## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `cited-substrate-churn-retention`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-27T04:16:41.976Z.

Extending the catalog 2026-07-27 — entry (28). The catalog runs (1)-(27) and is not restarted here.

(28) Evidence half-life conditioned on cited-substrate churn — invalidation as a first-class signal, distinct from recency.

The problem the existing entries cannot reach. Every temporal entry in this catalog scores an item by facts about the item: (1) ACT-R base-level activation decays by time since the item's own accesses, (20) segments eras from change points in item activity, (22) tracks identity flow across copy, split, merge and supersede, and the staleness clause in the scoring notes penalises aging WIP. All of them answer how old the record is. None answers whether the record is still true. Those are different questions and in this workspace they routinely disagree. An item whose body carries a measurement of a specific file, a benchmark number, a line reference, or a byte count is a claim about a substrate that keeps moving after the claim is written. A finding recorded against a file that has since been rewritten sixty times is stale no matter how recently the item was touched, and a finding recorded against a file nobody has edited since is still exactly true no matter how old it is. Serving the first as fresh and burying the second as old is the failure mode, and it is invisible to every signal in (1)-(27) because they all read item metadata and never read the substrate.

Why this workspace can compute it and a generic tracker cannot. pm already stores the dependency between claim and substrate: items carry linked files, linked docs and linked tests, each with a path, and the repository carries the commit history of those paths. The join is therefore available without any new capture: for an item i with linked artifacts A(i), and an observation instant t(i) taken as the history instant at which the citing text was written rather than the item's updated_at, the churn exposure is the change activity over A(i) in the interval from t(i) to now. Concretely churn(i) = sum over a in A(i) of w(a) * c(a, t(i), now), where c is the number of commits touching path a in the window and w(a) weights how load-bearing the citation is, with a linked test weighted above a linked doc because a test asserts behaviour while a doc describes it. A missing or deleted path is the maximal case, not a zero: the substrate did not merely change, it left.

The scoring shape. Keep the linear, explainable form entry (3) fixes, and add one term rather than modifying (1). Trust(i) = exp(-churn(i) / H) where H is a fitted half-life in churn units, and the served relevance multiplies the existing score by Trust(i). This composes rather than competes: (1) still answers how recently the item mattered, (28) answers how much of what it says can still be relied on, and an item can be simultaneously recent and untrustworthy or old and solid, which is precisely the distinction the current model collapses. The uncertainty machinery in (21) applies unchanged because H is a pooled estimate with a small-sample regime, and the write-time fold in (6) is where churn accumulates: a commit touching path a increments a per-path counter, so no read ever walks the repository log.

What it changes for the consumer. Three behaviours follow directly. First, the evidence-bearing items an agent is most likely to act on are ranked by whether their evidence survived, so a measured claim from three weeks ago about an untouched file outranks a restated claim from yesterday about a file under active rewrite. Second, the ranking explanation gains a term an agent can act on: not merely that an item scored low, but that it cites artifacts which have moved N times since the claim was written, which is an instruction to re-measure rather than to ignore. Third, it gives the corpus a maintenance signal it currently lacks — the set of items whose trust has decayed below a threshold is exactly the set whose findings should be re-verified before being cited, and today nothing in the system can name that set.

Boundaries against neighbouring entries, so this is not a re-spelling. (12) co-change coupling mining measures which artifacts move together in order to expand a candidate set; (28) measures how much one artifact moved after a specific claim in order to discount that claim, and is a per-item scalar rather than a pairwise association. (14) retrieval-conditioned contradiction gating fires when two retrieved items assert incompatible things; (28) fires with a single item and no contradiction present, because substrate motion is evidence of possible staleness without any second claim. (15) age-and-value-conditioned verbatim decay decides which bytes to compact away; (28) decides how much to trust bytes that are fully retained. (20) detects regime changes in item activity; (28) reads repository activity, which is a different series and moves when the tracker is idle.

Prerequisites and placement. The write-time fold (6) owns the per-path counter, the linked-artifact join is already public through the annotation and link primitives, and the fitted half-life H is a pm-atfm evaluation question rather than a free parameter. Nothing here requires a new capture surface, which is why it is proposed as an engine entry rather than as a memory subsystem candidate under the cognitive-memory ADR.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
